title: Rhinoplasty Guide: Types, Candidacy, Cost, Recovery and Results
metaTitle: Rhinoplasty Guide: Types, Cost, Recovery and Results
description: Rhinoplasty explained: open vs closed, candidacy, cost in India, recovery timeline and results. Book a consultation with Dr Vybhav Deraje, Bangalore.
card: Open vs closed Rhinoplasty, who it suits, a phase-by-phase recovery timeline, risks and what drives the cost in India.
intro: Thinking about changing the shape of your nose, or finally fixing a breathing problem that has bothered you for years? Rhinoplasty (nose reshaping surgery) can do both. It changes the size, shape or proportions of the nose by reshaping its bone and cartilage, and it can be combined with Septoplasty (straightening the inner wall of the nose) to improve airflow.

Most people return to desk work in about one to two weeks, but the final shape takes up to a year to settle. In this guide you will learn the main types of Rhinoplasty, who is a good candidate, what happens on the day, a realistic recovery timeline, the risks, and what drives Rhinoplasty cost in India.
takeaways: Nose reshaping surgery can improve appearance, breathing, or both. When the septum is also corrected, it is called Septorhinoplasty.
The two main approaches are open (a small incision under the tip) and closed (all incisions inside the nose).
Most people take one to two weeks off work. Visible bruising usually fades within two weeks.
Subtle swelling, especially at the tip, can take 6 to 12 months or longer to settle.
A typical uncomplicated case at this practice is approximately INR 1,50,000 to 2,00,000 plus GST.
A good result should look natural and suit your face, not a "standard" nose.

sections.heading: What is Rhinoplasty?

blocks.text: Rhinoplasty is a surgical procedure that reshapes the nose by modifying its bone, cartilage and soft tissue. It can reduce a hump, refine a wide or drooping tip, narrow the nostrils, raise a low bridge, correct a crooked nose, or improve breathing. It is performed by a qualified plastic surgeon under general or local anaesthesia with sedation.
Patients usually come with one of two goals, and often both:

items: **Cosmetic goals:** a dorsal hump (bump on the bridge), a wide or bulbous tip, a low bridge, asymmetry, or a nose that looks out of balance with the face.
**Functional goals:** blocked breathing from a deviated septum, collapsing nasal valves, or an old injury.

blocks.text: When breathing and shape are corrected together, the operation is called Septorhinoplasty. Treating both in one sitting means one anaesthetic and one recovery.

sections.heading: Types of Rhinoplasty

blocks.text: Primary vs revision Rhinoplasty

Primary Rhinoplasty is the first operation on the nose. Revision (secondary) surgery corrects or improves the result of an earlier surgery. Revision is usually more complex because of scar tissue and reduced cartilage, and surgeons often need to borrow cartilage from the ear or rib. Most surgeons advise waiting around a year after the first operation before considering revision, so the nose has fully settled.
Open vs closed Rhinoplasty: which is better?

Neither approach is better for everyone. The open technique gives the surgeon direct vision of the cartilage framework and suits complex tip work, revisions and grafting. Closed Rhinoplasty avoids an external scar and may have slightly less early swelling, which suits selected, more limited changes. Your anatomy and goals decide the approach.

head: Feature
Open approach
Closed approach
rows: Small incision across the columella (skin between the nostrils) plus incisions inside
Full, direct view of the cartilage
Complex tip work, grafting, revisions, crooked noses
Fine scar under the tip, usually inconspicuous once healed

blocks.text: Other terms you may hear

items: **Tip-plasty:** surgery limited to the nasal tip.
**Augmentation:** building up a low bridge using cartilage grafts or, in some cases, implants.
**Reduction:** reducing a hump or overall size.
**Non-surgical ("liquid") nose job:** fillers to camouflage small irregularities. It is temporary, cannot reduce size or fix breathing, and carries its own risks.

sections.heading: Indian nasal anatomy: why one size does not fit all

blocks.text: Many Indian patients have thicker nasal skin, a lower or softer bridge, wider nostrils and less natural tip support than the noses shown in Western textbooks. That matters because thick skin hides fine cartilage changes and holds swelling longer, so the surgeon may need to strengthen the tip framework rather than simply remove cartilage.
Good nose surgery respects your ethnic features. The aim is a nose that looks like it belongs on your face, not a copied celebrity nose.
How to avoid an "overdone" look

items: Ask for balance with your forehead, lips and chin, not a dramatic change in one feature.
Be wary of an overly pinched tip or a very scooped bridge. These can look operated and may also narrow the airway.
Discuss whether a modest chin change would improve your profile more than a large nose change.
Review computer imaging as a communication tool, not a promise.

sections.heading: Who is a good candidate for Rhinoplasty (and who is not)?

blocks.text: You may be a good candidate if you:

items: Are in good general health and a non-smoker, or willing to stop well before and after surgery
Have a specific concern you can describe, such as a hump, a drooping tip or blocked breathing
Have realistic expectations and understand that improvement, not perfection, is the goal
Have finished facial growth, usually by the mid to late teens

blocks.text: It may be wise to wait, or not proceed, if you:

items: Are still growing, unless the surgery is for significant breathing problems
Are seeking surgery because of pressure from someone else
Expect the operation to fix wider personal or relationship issues

Have intense distress about a minor or barely visible feature. A sensitive, honest conversation about body dysmorphic disorder (a condition causing excessive preoccupation with perceived flaws) may be more helpful than surgery.
Have uncontrolled medical conditions, or take blood thinners that cannot be safely paused

sections.heading: The procedure, step by step

items: **Consultation:** your surgeon examines the outside and inside of your nose, checks breathing, discusses goals and takes standard photographs.
**Planning:** you agree on the changes, the approach (open or closed), whether Septoplasty is needed, and grafting options.
**Pre-operative tests:** routine blood tests and a fitness check for anaesthesia. You will be advised which medicines and supplements to stop.
**Anaesthesia:** most nose surgery is done under general anaesthesia. Some limited procedures use local anaesthesia with sedation.
**The surgery:** typically takes around two to four hours, depending on complexity. The surgeon reshapes bone and cartilage, then closes the incisions.
**After surgery:** a small splint is placed on the nose. Soft internal splints or packing may be used. Many patients go home the same day or after one night.

sections.heading: Nose job recovery: a phase-by-phase timeline

blocks.text: Healing happens in stages. The NHS notes that it can take up to six months for swelling to go completely, and the bridge usually settles before the tip. Your surgeon's instructions always come first.

head: Phase
What is normal
Typical restrictions and milestones
rows: Stuffy nose, swelling and bruising around the eyes, mild to moderate discomfort
Sleep with head raised. No blowing the nose. Splint usually removed around day 7
Most bruising fades. Nose looks swollen and may feel stiff or numb
Desk work often possible from week 2. No contact sports. Avoid glasses resting on the bridge until advised
Gradual return to full exercise as your surgeon allows. Protect the nose from sun
Residual tip swelling settles, particularly in thick skin
Final review. Results are judged at around 12 months

blocks.text: When can you return to work, driving and exercise?

items: **Work:** desk jobs usually after one to two weeks.
**Driving:** once you are off strong painkillers and can turn your head comfortably, often around one week. Confirm with your surgeon.
**Exercise:** light walking from the first days. Cardio is usually reintroduced after a few weeks, and contact sports later still.

sections.heading: Risks and complications of Rhinoplasty

blocks.text: Nose surgery is generally safe when performed by a qualified plastic surgeon in an accredited hospital, but every operation carries risk. Possible complications include:

items: Bleeding, including nosebleeds in the first days
Infection
Reactions to anaesthesia
Prolonged swelling or numbness of the tip
Difficulty breathing through the nose
Altered sense of smell, usually temporary
Asymmetry or an irregular contour
Visible scar under the tip after the open approach, which is uncommon
Septal perforation (a hole in the septum), which is rare
Dissatisfaction with the result and the possibility of revision surgery

blocks.text: Your surgeon will explain how these apply to you before you sign consent.

sections.heading: Rhinoplasty cost in India: what affects the price?

blocks.text: Prices vary widely because quotes include very different things. The main cost drivers are:

items: **Surgeon's training and experience** with primary and revision nose surgery
**Complexity:** tip-only work costs less than Septorhinoplasty or revision with rib cartilage
**Hospital and stay:** day care vs overnight, and the hospital category
**Anaesthesia:** general anaesthesia and the anaesthetist's fee
**City:** metro cities such as Bangalore, Mumbai and Delhi tend to cost more
**Inclusions:** tests, medicines, splints and follow-up visits

blocks.text: As an approximate guide, this practice lists the procedure for a typical uncomplicated case at INR 1,50,000 to 2,00,000 plus GST. Pre-operative tests and medicines after discharge are usually extra. Your individual estimate is confirmed after assessment. See our [treatment costs page](/treatment-costs) for current details.
Insurance may cover functional surgery such as Septoplasty when it is medically needed, but purely cosmetic nose reshaping is usually not covered. Check with your insurer.

sections.heading: Rhinoplasty before and after: what results can you expect?

blocks.text: A successful result is a nose that breathes well and looks in balance with your face. Expect improvement rather than perfection, since every face is slightly asymmetric. Early photos at two weeks do not show the final shape. Ask to see before and after photos of comparable noses at your consultation, taken with consent.
Results are long-lasting. The nose will still age naturally with the rest of your face.

sections.heading: When to call your surgeon

blocks.text: Contact your surgeon or hospital promptly if you have:

items: Fever above 38 degrees C, or chills
Heavy bleeding that does not stop with gentle pressure and head elevation
Increasing pain, redness or swelling after the first few days
Pus or a foul smell from the nose or incision
Sudden, severe one-sided swelling
Calf pain or swelling, chest pain or breathlessness. Seek emergency care
Changes in vision or a severe headache

sections.heading: Questions to ask at your Rhinoplasty consultation

items: Are you a qualified plastic surgeon, and how often do you perform primary and revision nose surgery?
Do you recommend the open or closed approach for me, and why?
Will my breathing be assessed and treated at the same time?
How will my skin thickness affect the result?
Will you need cartilage grafts, and from where?
Which hospital will I be treated in, and who gives the anaesthetic?
What exactly is included in the quoted cost?
What is your policy if revision is needed?
Can I see before and after photos of patients with similar noses?

sections.heading: Is Rhinoplasty right for you?

blocks.text: Rhinoplasty can improve how your nose looks and how well you breathe, but the best outcomes come from careful planning, a natural goal and patience while swelling settles. If you are considering Rhinoplasty in Bangalore, learn more on our [Rhinoplasty surgery page](/rhinoplasty-surgery-bangalore) or explore other [facial plastic surgery procedures](/face-plastic-surgery-bangalore). You can read about [Dr Vybhav Deraje's background](/aboutus) and, when you are ready, [book a consultation](/contact-us) to talk through your goals honestly.

faqs.q: How much does Rhinoplasty cost in India?
faqs.a: Rhinoplasty cost in India depends on complexity, the surgeon, the hospital and the city. At this practice, a typical uncomplicated case is approximately INR 1,50,000 to 2,00,000 plus GST, with tests and some medicines billed separately. Revision Rhinoplasty and cases needing rib cartilage usually cost more. An exact estimate is given after assessment.

faqs.q: Is Rhinoplasty painful?
faqs.a: Most people describe recovery as uncomfortable rather than very painful. The first few days bring a blocked nose, pressure and tenderness, which are usually controlled with prescribed painkillers. Discomfort typically eases noticeably within the first week. The stuffiness from swelling often bothers patients more than pain does.

faqs.q: How long does it take for the nose to settle after Rhinoplasty?
faqs.a: Most bruising fades within two weeks, and the nose looks presentable to others within a few weeks. Subtle swelling, especially at the tip, can take 6 to 12 months or longer to settle, particularly with thick skin or open Rhinoplasty. Final results are usually judged at around one year.

faqs.q: What is the best age for Rhinoplasty?
faqs.a: Cosmetic nose surgery is usually done after the nose has finished growing, typically in the mid to late teens and often later for boys. There is no upper age limit if you are healthy. Surgery for significant breathing problems or injury may sometimes be considered earlier, after careful assessment.

faqs.q: Will Rhinoplasty fix my breathing?
faqs.a: Nose surgery can improve breathing when the cause is structural, such as a deviated septum or weak nasal valves. This usually needs Septoplasty or valve support, performed as Septorhinoplasty. Breathing problems caused by allergies or sinus disease may need medical treatment instead, so a proper assessment before surgery is important.

faqs.q: Is open or closed Rhinoplasty better?
faqs.a: Neither is better for everyone. The open approach gives a full view of the cartilage and suits complex tip work, grafting and revision. Closed Rhinoplasty avoids an external scar and suits selected, more limited changes. Your surgeon should explain which approach suits your anatomy and goals.

faqs.q: Can Rhinoplasty go wrong?
faqs.a: Like any operation, it carries risks, including bleeding, infection, breathing difficulty, asymmetry and dissatisfaction with the shape. A proportion of patients choose revision surgery later. Choosing a qualified plastic surgeon, setting realistic goals and following aftercare instructions closely help reduce, but cannot remove, these risks.

faqs.q: When can I wear glasses after nose surgery?
faqs.a: Many surgeons advise avoiding glasses resting on the bridge for around four to six weeks, especially if the nasal bones were moved. You can tape glasses to the forehead or use contact lenses in the meantime. Follow your own surgeon's instructions, as advice depends on the procedure performed.

disclaimer: This article is for general education only. It is not medical advice or a diagnosis, and it does not replace a consultation with a qualified plastic surgeon. Results vary from person to person.

references.label: American Society of Plastic Surgeons, Rhinoplasty
Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, Rhinoplasty discharge advice

title: Breast Augmentation Guide: Implants vs Fat Transfer, Cost and Recovery
metaTitle: Breast Augmentation: Implants vs Fat, Cost and Recovery
description: Breast Augmentation explained: implants vs Fat Transfer, sizing, cost in India and recovery. Book a consultation with Dr Vybhav Deraje in Bangalore.
card: Implants or your own fat: how the two compare, choosing a size, recovery, long-term implant checks and cost in India.
intro: Wondering whether implants or your own fat would suit you better? Breast Augmentation (surgery to increase breast size or restore volume) can be done either way. Implants give a larger, more predictable increase. Fat Transfer gives a smaller, softer change and needs enough spare fat elsewhere on the body.

The right choice depends on your frame, your existing breast tissue and how much change you want. This guide explains both options, how to choose size, what recovery looks like, the risks, and what affects Breast Augmentation cost in India.
takeaways: Implants can add a defined amount of volume. Fat Transfer usually adds a modest increase and may need more than one session.
Breast implants are not lifetime devices. Many people need further surgery at some point.
Silicone implants need periodic checks for silent rupture, as advised by your surgeon.
Most people return to desk work in about one to two weeks, with no heavy lifting for around six weeks.
A typical uncomplicated case at this practice is approximately INR 1,75,000 to 2,00,000 plus GST with silicone implants, or INR 1,50,000 to 1,75,000 plus GST with Fat Transfer.

sections.heading: What is Breast Augmentation?

blocks.text: Breast Augmentation, also called Augmentation Mammoplasty, is surgery to increase the size, fullness or symmetry of the breasts. It uses either breast implants (silicone or saline) or Fat Transfer (your own fat, moved by Liposuction). People choose it for smaller breasts, asymmetry, or volume loss after pregnancy, breastfeeding or weight loss.
It does not lift sagging breasts on its own. If the nipple sits low, a Breast Lift (Mastopexy) may be needed as well.

sections.heading: Breast implants vs Fat Transfer: which is better for you?

blocks.text: Neither option is better for everyone. Implants suit people who want a clear increase in size and have limited spare fat. Fat Transfer suits people who want a subtle change, have enough donor fat and would like to avoid an implant. Your surgeon will assess your tissue, skin quality and goals before advising.

head: Factor
Breast implants
Fat Transfer
rows: Modest, often around one cup size or less per session
Soft, especially with good tissue cover
Natural, as it is your own tissue
Short incision, usually under the breast fold
Slimming of donor areas such as the abdomen or thighs
Long-lasting, but may need replacement over time
Surviving fat is long-term, but some is reabsorbed
Possible exchange or revision in future
Fat loss, oil cysts, firm lumps (fat necrosis)

sections.heading: Breast implants explained

blocks.text: Silicone vs saline implants

items: **Silicone gel implants** are filled with cohesive gel and are widely used in India. Many people feel they look and feel more like breast tissue. A rupture may be "silent", so periodic imaging is advised.
**Saline implants** are filled with sterile salt water. If they rupture, the implant deflates visibly and the saline is absorbed by the body. They can show more rippling in slim patients.

blocks.text: Shape, surface and profile

Implants come in round or anatomical (teardrop) shapes and in different profiles (how far they project). Surface texture also matters. The FDA has linked breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL, a rare immune system cancer) mainly to textured implants. Ask your surgeon which surface they use and why.
Placement: above or below the muscle?

items: **Subglandular (above the muscle):** may suit people with enough natural breast tissue. Recovery can be easier.
**Submuscular or dual plane (partly below the muscle):** gives more soft-tissue cover over the implant, which can reduce visible edges and rippling in slim patients.

blocks.text: Incision options

items: **Inframammary:** in the crease under the breast. The most common choice, with good access and a hidden scar.
**Periareolar:** along the lower edge of the areola. May have a higher chance of affecting nipple sensation or breastfeeding.
**Transaxillary:** in the armpit, leaving no scar on the breast itself.

blocks.text: How to choose breast implant size

Size is about proportion, not a cup letter. A good plan starts with measurements of your chest width, breast base diameter, skin stretch and tissue thickness. An implant wider than your natural breast base can look unnatural and stretch tissue over time.

items: Bring photos of results you like, and ones you do not.
Try implant sizers in a fitted bra during consultation.
Think about your lifestyle, sport and clothing.
Remember that larger implants place more long-term strain on tissue.

sections.heading: Fat Transfer Breast Augmentation explained

blocks.text: Fat Transfer (autologous fat grafting) uses Liposuction to take fat from areas such as the abdomen, flanks or thighs. The fat is purified and injected in small amounts into the breasts.
It suits people who:

items: Want a modest, natural increase or correction of mild asymmetry
Have enough donor fat. Very slim patients may not
Have good skin quality and no significant sagging
Accept that some transferred fat is reabsorbed in the first few months, and a second session may be needed

blocks.text: Fat Transfer is also used to fine-tune implant results, for example softening the upper edge of an implant. Learn more about [Liposuction](/liposuction-surgery-bangalore), which forms the first stage of this procedure.

sections.heading: Who is a good candidate (and who is not)?

blocks.text: You may be a good candidate if you:

items: Are in good physical health and have a stable weight
Have finished growing and are an adult
Are not pregnant or breastfeeding. Most surgeons advise waiting several months after you stop
Have realistic expectations and are choosing surgery for yourself

blocks.text: Augmentation may not be right for you now if you:

items: Plan a pregnancy soon, as breasts often change again afterwards
Have an undiagnosed breast lump or are due for screening. Get this checked first
Smoke and are unable to stop around the time of surgery
Have uncontrolled diabetes, a bleeding disorder or active infection
Feel pressured by a partner, family or social media

sections.heading: The procedure: what to expect

items: **Consultation:** examination, measurements, discussion of implants vs Fat Transfer, and a review of your breast health history.
**Planning:** choosing implant type, size, placement and incision, or mapping donor areas for Fat Transfer.
**Pre-operative tests:** blood tests and an anaesthesia check. A breast ultrasound or mammogram may be advised depending on your age and history.
**Anaesthesia:** Breast Augmentation is usually performed under general anaesthesia.
**Surgery:** implant augmentation typically takes about one to two hours. Fat Transfer can take longer because Liposuction is done first.
**Going home:** many patients go home the same day or after one night, wearing a supportive surgical bra.

sections.heading: Breast Augmentation recovery timeline

blocks.text: Everyone heals differently, and your own surgeon's plan comes first. As a general guide:

head: Phase
What is normal
Typical restrictions and milestones
rows: Tightness, soreness, swelling; chest may feel heavy, especially with implants under the muscle
Rest, short walks, support bra day and night, no lifting
Pain eases; implants may sit high and firm
Desk work usually from 1 to 2 weeks; driving when you can brake and turn safely
Swelling settles; implants begin to "drop and fluff"
Gradual return to exercise; no heavy lifting or chest workouts until cleared, often around 6 weeks
Shape settles; scars flatten and fade
Final result usually assessed from about 3 to 6 months; Fat Transfer volume stabilises over several months

blocks.text: Scars are typically pink at first and fade over 12 to 18 months. Your surgeon may recommend silicone gel or sheets and sun protection.

sections.heading: Risks and complications

blocks.text: All surgery carries risk. Possible complications of Breast Augmentation include:

items: Bleeding or haematoma (a collection of blood)
Infection
Changes in nipple or breast sensation
Capsular contracture (scar tissue tightening around an implant, causing firmness or distortion)
Implant rupture, leakage, rippling or malposition
BIA-ALCL, which is rare
Systemic symptoms some patients attribute to implants, often called breast implant illness
With Fat Transfer: fat loss, oil cysts, calcifications and fat necrosis
Asymmetry or a result that differs from your expectations

blocks.text: In the USA, the FDA requires breast implant labelling to carry a boxed warning stating that implants are not lifetime devices and that the chance of complications increases over time. Ask your surgeon to go through these risks with you before you consent.
How long do breast implants last?

Breast implants do not have a fixed expiry date, but they are not designed to last a lifetime. Many people need an exchange or removal at some point, for reasons such as rupture, capsular contracture or a wish to change size. For silicone implants, the FDA recommends a first ultrasound or MRI 5 to 6 years after surgery and then every 2 to 3 years, even without symptoms.
Breastfeeding and breast screening

Many women can breastfeed after augmentation, particularly when the implant is placed through an incision under the breast. Fat Transfer does not prevent breastfeeding. Always tell your radiographer you have implants or fat grafting, as mammograms may need extra views.

sections.heading: Breast Augmentation cost in India

blocks.text: Breast Augmentation cost in India depends on:

items: The surgeon's training and experience
The technique: implants, Fat Transfer, or a combination
Implant brand, type and surface
Hospital category and length of stay
Anaesthesia fees
City, with metros such as Bangalore generally higher
Inclusions such as surgical bras, compression garments, tests and follow-up

blocks.text: As an approximate guide, this practice lists a typical uncomplicated case at INR 1,75,000 to 2,00,000 plus GST with silicone implants, and INR 1,50,000 to 1,75,000 plus GST with Fat Transfer. Pre-operative tests, medicines after discharge and compression garments are usually billed separately. See our [treatment costs page](/treatment-costs) for current information.

sections.heading: When to call your surgeon

blocks.text: Contact your surgeon promptly if you notice:

items: Fever above 38 degrees C, or chills
One breast suddenly becoming much larger, tense or more painful than the other
Spreading redness, warmth or discharge from an incision
A wound that opens
Calf pain or swelling, chest pain or breathlessness. Seek emergency care
Later on: new swelling, a lump, a change in shape or firmness months or years after surgery

sections.heading: Questions to ask at your consultation

items: Are you a qualified plastic surgeon, and how often do you perform Breast Augmentation?
Am I better suited to implants, Fat Transfer or a combination, and why?
Which implant brand, surface and shape do you recommend?
What size range suits my chest width and tissue?
Above or below the muscle, and which incision?
What is the plan if I develop capsular contracture or rupture?
How will this affect breastfeeding and future mammograms?
What does the quoted cost include?

sections.heading: Is Breast Augmentation right for you?

blocks.text: Breast Augmentation can restore volume or improve balance, but it is a long-term commitment, especially with implants. The best decisions come from an honest assessment of your anatomy, goals and future plans. Read more on our [Breast Augmentation surgery page](/breast-augmentation-surgery-bangalore), explore other [breast surgery options](/breast-plastic-surgeon-bangalore), and learn about [Dr Vybhav Deraje](/aboutus). When you are ready, [book a consultation in Bangalore](/contact-us).

faqs.q: What is the cost of Breast Augmentation in India?
faqs.a: Breast Augmentation cost in India varies with technique, implant type, hospital and city. At this practice, a typical uncomplicated case is approximately INR 1,75,000 to 2,00,000 plus GST with silicone implants and INR 1,50,000 to 1,75,000 plus GST with Fat Transfer. Tests, medicines and garments are usually extra.

faqs.q: Which is better, breast implants or Fat Transfer?
faqs.a: Neither is better for everyone. Implants suit people who want a noticeable, predictable increase. Fat Transfer suits those who want a subtle change, have enough spare fat and prefer to avoid an implant. Some patients benefit from a combination. Your tissue, frame and goals should guide the decision.

faqs.q: How long do breast implants last?
faqs.a: Breast implants are not lifetime devices. Many last for many years, but the chance of needing further surgery rises over time due to rupture, capsular contracture or a desire to change size. For silicone implants, the FDA recommends imaging at 5 to 6 years after surgery, then every 2 to 3 years.

faqs.q: Can I breastfeed after Breast Augmentation?
faqs.a: Many women can breastfeed after Breast Augmentation, though it cannot be guaranteed. Incisions under the breast fold and implants placed behind the muscle may interfere less with milk ducts. Fat Transfer does not usually affect breastfeeding. Discuss your future plans with your surgeon before choosing a technique.

faqs.q: Silicone vs saline implants: which is safer?
faqs.a: Both silicone and saline implants are approved and widely studied, and each has trade-offs. Silicone often feels more natural but a rupture can be silent, so regular imaging is advised. Saline deflates visibly if it ruptures and the fluid is absorbed. Your surgeon will explain what suits your tissue.

faqs.q: How long is recovery after Breast Augmentation?
faqs.a: Most people return to desk work within one to two weeks. Heavy lifting and upper body exercise are usually avoided for around six weeks. Swelling settles over several weeks, and the final shape is usually visible after three to six months. Your surgeon will give a personal recovery plan.

faqs.q: Does Fat Transfer to the breast last?
faqs.a: Fat that survives the first few months after transfer usually behaves like normal body fat and is long-lasting. However, a portion of the injected fat is naturally reabsorbed, so results can be less predictable than implants. Weight gain or loss will also change the size of the transferred fat.

disclaimer: This article is for general education only. It is not medical advice or a diagnosis, and it does not replace a consultation with a qualified plastic surgeon. Results vary from person to person.

title: Diastasis Recti After Pregnancy: Exercises vs Surgical Repair
metaTitle: Diastasis Recti After Pregnancy: Exercises vs Surgery
description: Diastasis Recti explained: symptoms, self-check, exercises vs surgical repair and timing. Book an assessment with Dr Vybhav Deraje in Bangalore.
card: How to check for abdominal separation, what physiotherapy can and cannot change, and when surgical repair is worth discussing.
intro: Still seeing a soft bulge or "pooch" months after your baby was born, even though you have lost the pregnancy weight? It may be Diastasis Recti (separation of the abdominal muscles). It is very common after pregnancy and is nothing to feel embarrassed about.

For many women, a supervised physiotherapy programme improves core strength and symptoms. When the gap stays wide, the abdominal wall stays weak, or there is loose skin or a hernia, surgical repair can restore the muscles. This guide explains how to tell the difference and how to decide.
takeaways: Diastasis Recti is a widening of the midline tissue (linea alba) between the two "six-pack" muscles.
A gap wider than about 2 cm is commonly used to diagnose it.
Many cases improve in the first months after birth, but some persist a year or more later.
Guided exercise improves strength and function. It cannot remove loose skin and may not close a wide, stretched gap.
Surgical repair (muscle plication) is usually done with a Tummy Tuck once you have finished having children.
Get assessed before starting any programme.

sections.heading: What is Diastasis Recti?

blocks.text: Diastasis Recti is the separation of the left and right rectus abdominis muscles (the vertical "six-pack" muscles) caused by stretching and thinning of the linea alba, the band of connective tissue that joins them. It happens because the growing uterus stretches the abdominal wall. Cleveland Clinic notes that a gap wider than 2 centimetres is commonly used to diagnose it.
The muscles themselves are not torn. The connecting tissue has stretched and may have lost some of its tension.

sections.heading: Who gets abdominal separation after pregnancy?

blocks.text: Abdominal separation after pregnancy is the most common form. Risk is higher if you:

items: Have had more than one pregnancy, especially close together
Carried twins or triplets, or a large baby
Were pregnant over the age of 35
Have had large weight changes

blocks.text: Abdominal separation is not limited to women. Men can develop it too, usually from central weight gain or repeated heavy straining. It can also appear in newborns, where it usually resolves on its own.
How common is it?

A Norwegian study of first-time mothers found diastasis in around 60 percent of women at six weeks after birth and about a third at 12 months. Many women improve naturally in the first year. Others keep a gap long term.

sections.heading: Diastasis Recti symptoms

blocks.text: Common symptoms include:

items: A bulge or ridge down the middle of the abdomen, especially when you sit up or strain
A "pregnant look" that persists despite weight loss
A soft, doming area above or below the belly button
A feeling of core weakness when lifting or carrying your baby
Lower back pain or poor posture

blocks.text: Some women also have pelvic floor symptoms such as leaking urine. These are related but separate problems and deserve their own assessment.

sections.heading: How to check for Diastasis Recti at home

blocks.text: This simple check gives a rough idea only. It is not a diagnosis.

items: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Place your fingertips across your midline, just above the belly button.
Gently lift your head and shoulders a little, as in a small curl.
Feel for a gap between the muscle edges, and how many fingers fit.
Repeat just below the belly button and a few centimetres higher.
Notice how deep and soft the gap feels, not just how wide.

blocks.text: If two or more fingers fit, or you see doming, ask your doctor or a women's health physiotherapist to examine you. An ultrasound may be used to measure the gap and check for a hernia. Stop if you feel pain.

sections.heading: Why a gap alone is not always a problem

blocks.text: Width is only part of the story. What matters more is whether the midline tissue can create tension when you engage your core. A woman with a 2.5 cm gap and a firm, supportive midline may have no symptoms. Someone with a narrower but soft, deep gap may feel weak and see doming.
That is why treatment should focus on function, symptoms and your goals, not a number alone.

sections.heading: Diastasis Recti exercises: what physiotherapy can and cannot do

blocks.text: For most women, a guided programme with a physiotherapist trained in postnatal care is the right first step. These exercises focus on:

items: **Breathing and pressure management:** coordinating breath with core engagement
**Deep core activation:** training the transversus abdominis (the deep corset muscle)
**Pelvic floor work:** working together with the deep core
**Gradual loading:** slowly adding everyday and gym movements as control improves
**Posture and lifting technique:** for carrying babies, car seats and shopping

blocks.text: A review in Frontiers in Surgery (Jessen et al., 2019) found that conservative options include exercise, posture education and support garments, but that the quality of evidence is limited and no international guideline exists.
Exercises to avoid at first
Until you have been assessed, avoid unsupervised:

items: Crunches, sit-ups and double leg lifts
Full planks or advanced Pilates moves that cause doming
Heavy lifting with breath-holding
Getting up from lying straight forward. Roll to your side instead

blocks.text: These are not "banned forever". They simply need to be reintroduced with good control. Do not start any programme without checking with your doctor, and follow your physiotherapist's plan.
What exercise cannot do

Exercise strengthens muscles and improves control. It cannot remove loose, stretched skin, and it may not shorten a linea alba that has stretched significantly. If you still have significant symptoms or bulging after a consistent, supervised programme of several months, surgery may be worth discussing.

sections.heading: Diastasis Recti surgery: how the muscles are repaired

blocks.text: The operation is called rectus plication. The surgeon stitches the stretched midline tissue back together, bringing the muscles closer and firming the abdominal wall. The stitches are permanent and act as an internal corset.
Repair with a Tummy Tuck

Most cosmetic repairs are done as part of a [Tummy Tuck (Abdominoplasty)](/tummy-tuck-abdominoplasty-bangalore). Through a low incision that often runs along or near a C-section scar, the surgeon repairs the muscles, removes loose skin and fat, and repositions the belly button. Liposuction may be added for shaping. If you have had a caesarean delivery, read our guide to [Tummy Tuck after a C-section](/blog/tummy-tuck-after-c-section).
Repair without a Tummy Tuck

If skin is tight and the main issue is the muscle gap, minimally invasive or endoscopic repair may be an option in selected patients. These are usually done by surgeons with specific training in abdominal wall repair.
Diastasis Recti and hernia: what is the overlap?

Diastasis Recti is not a hernia, because the midline tissue is stretched but intact. However, an umbilical hernia (a weakness at the belly button through which tissue can push) often occurs alongside it. If one is found, it is usually repaired during the same operation.

sections.heading: Exercises vs surgery: a side-by-side comparison

head: Factor
Guided exercise and physiotherapy
Surgical repair (with or without Tummy Tuck)
rows: Mild to moderate gap, function and symptom improvement
Persistent wide gap, bulging, loose skin, hernia
Midline tightened with stitches; skin and fat removed if Tummy Tuck
Weeks to months of regular practice
Single operation, then several weeks of recovery
Usually 2 to 6 weeks off normal activity
Surgical and anaesthetic risks, scar, seroma, recurrence
Best done after completing your family

sections.heading: When is the right time for surgical repair?

blocks.text: Timing matters. Most plastic surgeons advise:

items: **Finishing your family first:** another pregnancy can stretch the repair again.
**Waiting after birth:** usually at least 6 to 12 months after delivery, so your body has recovered.
**Stopping breastfeeding:** and allowing a few months for breast and body changes to settle.
**Reaching a stable weight:** close to your goal, with a healthy lifestyle you can maintain.
**Trying physiotherapy first:** this builds strength that also helps after surgery.

sections.heading: Who is a good candidate for Diastasis Recti surgery (and who is not)?

blocks.text: You may be a good candidate if you:

items: Have a confirmed diastasis with ongoing bulging or weakness after physiotherapy
Have loose skin or a hernia as well
Have completed childbearing and are at a stable weight
Are healthy and a non-smoker

blocks.text: Surgery may not be right for you now if you:

items: Plan another pregnancy
Are still within the first months after delivery or still breastfeeding
Have significant weight still to lose
Have uncontrolled diabetes, heart or lung conditions, or a clotting history that has not been assessed

sections.heading: Recovery after Diastasis Recti repair

blocks.text: With a Tummy Tuck, recovery is a gradual process. As a general guide only:

items: **Week 1:** walking little and often, bending slightly at the waist, drains if used, compression garment
**Weeks 2 to 4:** many return to desk work around 2 weeks; no lifting heavier than your baby until cleared
**Weeks 6 to 8:** gradual return to exercise as advised; core work is reintroduced carefully
**Months 3 to 12:** swelling settles and the scar matures

blocks.text: Lifting a toddler is one of the hardest parts of recovery. Plan help at home for the first few weeks.

sections.heading: Diastasis Recti surgery cost in India: what affects it?

blocks.text: Muscle repair is usually priced as part of a Tummy Tuck, so the cost depends on what is done alongside it. The main cost drivers are:

items: Whether repair is combined with a full or Mini Tummy Tuck, Liposuction or hernia repair
The surgeon's training and experience
Hospital category, length of stay and anaesthesia
City, with Bangalore and other metros generally higher
Compression garments, tests and medicines

blocks.text: As an approximate guide, this practice lists a typical uncomplicated Tummy Tuck at INR 3,50,000 to 4,50,000 plus GST. See the [treatment costs page](/treatment-costs) for current details.

sections.heading: Risks and complications

blocks.text: Possible risks of surgical repair include bleeding, infection, seroma (fluid build-up), delayed wound healing, numbness of the lower abdomen, a visible scar, blood clots in the legs or lungs, and recurrence of the gap, especially after another pregnancy. Your surgeon will explain how these apply to you.

sections.heading: When to see a doctor

blocks.text: Seek prompt medical advice if you have:

items: A painful, hard or non-reducible bulge, especially with vomiting. This can signal a trapped hernia and needs urgent care
After surgery: fever, spreading redness, wound opening, sudden one-sided swelling
Calf pain or swelling, chest pain or breathlessness. Seek emergency care

sections.heading: Questions to ask at your consultation

items: How wide is my gap, and is there a hernia?
Would physiotherapy alone help me, or do I need repair?
Will you repair the muscles as part of a Tummy Tuck, or separately?
How long should I wait after delivery and breastfeeding?
What happens if I become pregnant after surgery?
Which hospital, what anaesthesia, and what does the cost include?

sections.heading: Is Diastasis Recti surgery right for you?

blocks.text: This condition is common, often improves with time and the right exercises, and is not something to rush. If bulging or weakness persists after a proper programme, surgical repair can be a sensible next step once your family is complete. Explore our [body contouring procedures](/body-plastic-surgeon-bangalore), learn about [Dr Vybhav Deraje](/aboutus), check [how to prepare for your visit](/patient-resources), and [book an assessment](/contact-us) when you are ready.

faqs.q: Can Diastasis Recti heal on its own?
faqs.a: Diastasis Recti often improves on its own in the first months after birth as the abdominal wall recovers. Many women see a narrower gap by six months to a year. However, some keep a gap long term. A physiotherapy programme can support recovery, and persistent cases can be assessed for surgery.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have Diastasis Recti?
faqs.a: Signs include a midline bulge or ridge when you sit up, a persistent "pregnant look" and core weakness. A home finger check can suggest a gap, but a doctor or physiotherapist should confirm it. An ultrasound can measure the separation and check for an umbilical hernia at the same time.

faqs.q: What exercises should I avoid with Diastasis Recti?
faqs.a: Avoid unsupervised crunches, sit-ups, double leg lifts and movements that make your midline dome or bulge, at least until you are assessed. Heavy lifting with breath-holding also adds strain. A physiotherapist can teach safer deep core exercises and help you reintroduce harder moves with good control.

faqs.q: Can you fix Diastasis Recti years after pregnancy?
faqs.a: Yes. Diastasis Recti can be treated years after pregnancy. Exercise can still improve strength and symptoms at any stage. If the gap remains wide or there is loose skin, surgical repair, usually with a Tummy Tuck, can be done whenever you have completed your family and are in good health.

faqs.q: Is Diastasis Recti the same as a hernia?
faqs.a: No. Diastasis Recti is a stretching of the connective tissue between the abdominal muscles, which remains intact. A hernia is a defect through which tissue pushes. The two often occur together, especially at the belly button, and both can be repaired during the same operation.

faqs.q: Is Diastasis Recti surgery covered by insurance in India?
faqs.a: Coverage varies. Repair done mainly for cosmetic reasons, such as with a Tummy Tuck, is usually not covered. If a hernia is present or the repair is medically necessary, part of the treatment may be covered depending on your policy. Check with your insurer and ask the clinic for documentation.

faqs.q: Can men get Diastasis Recti?
faqs.a: Yes. Men can develop Diastasis Recti, usually from central weight gain, heavy straining or improper lifting. It often appears as a ridge down the middle of the abdomen. Assessment, weight management and core training are the first steps, with surgery considered when there is a hernia or significant symptoms.

disclaimer: This article is for general education only. It is not medical advice or a diagnosis, and it does not replace an examination by a qualified doctor or physiotherapist. Individual treatment plans vary, and results differ from person to person.

Hall H, Sanjaghsaz H. Diastasis Recti Rehabilitation. StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf)

title: Tummy Tuck After C-Section: Timing, Scar and Results
metaTitle: Tummy Tuck After C-Section: Timing, Scar and Results
description: Tummy Tuck after C section: when to have it, what happens to the scar, recovery and cost in India. Book a consultation with Dr Vybhav Deraje.
card: When to have it, what happens to the caesarean scar, full vs mini Tummy Tuck, recovery and cost in India.
intro: Many women notice a fold of skin hanging over their caesarean scar, a soft lower belly or a midline bulge that does not change with diet and exercise. A Tummy Tuck after C section can help. Abdominoplasty (Tummy Tuck surgery) removes loose skin and fat, repairs separated muscles and, in most cases, removes or replaces the old C-section scar.

Most surgeons advise waiting at least 6 to 12 months after delivery, finishing breastfeeding and reaching a stable weight first. This guide explains the timing, what happens to your scar, full vs Mini Tummy Tuck, recovery, risks and cost in India.
takeaways: A Tummy Tuck after C-section can remove the overhang ("shelf"), tighten the abdominal wall and remove or incorporate the C-section scar.
It is usually best done once you have completed your family, finished breastfeeding and reached a stable weight.
The new scar sits low, in a similar position to a C-section scar, but is usually longer.
Most people take around 2 to 6 weeks off work depending on their job, and avoid strenuous exercise for about 6 weeks.
A typical uncomplicated Tummy Tuck at this practice is approximately INR 3,50,000 to 4,50,000 plus GST.

sections.heading: What is a Tummy Tuck after C-section?

blocks.text: A Tummy Tuck after C-section, also called Abdominoplasty after cesarean delivery, is a Tummy Tuck performed on someone who has previously had a caesarean. It removes excess lower abdominal skin and fat, tightens the stretched abdominal muscles, and places a new low scar that usually replaces the C-section scar. It is a body contouring operation, not a weight-loss treatment.

A C-section and a Tummy Tuck are very different operations. A caesarean opens the abdominal wall and uterus to deliver the baby. A Tummy Tuck works on the skin, fat and muscle layer in front, without entering the abdomen.

sections.heading: Why does a C-section overhang form?

blocks.text: The "C-section shelf" or overhang is a fold of skin and fat that sits above the caesarean scar. It forms because the scar tethers the skin to deeper tissue while the skin above it remains loose after pregnancy. Stretched skin, stubborn lower belly fat and separated muscles all add to it.
Exercise strengthens muscle but cannot shorten stretched skin or release a tethered scar. That is why C section overhang surgery is one of the most common reasons women ask about a Tummy Tuck.

sections.heading: How long after a C-section can you have a Tummy Tuck?

blocks.text: Most plastic surgeons recommend waiting at least 6 to 12 months after a C-section before a Tummy Tuck. This allows the uterus, abdominal wall and scar to heal fully, weight to stabilise and breastfeeding to end. Waiting also lets you see how much your body recovers naturally with time and physiotherapy.
Before you plan surgery, it helps to have:

items: **Completed your family:** a future pregnancy will stretch the skin and the muscle repair again.
**Finished breastfeeding:** usually with a gap of a few months afterwards.
**A stable weight:** close to your goal and maintained for several months.
**Recovered physically and emotionally:** caring for a young child while recovering from major surgery needs planning and support at home.
**Tried a core programme:** guided postnatal physiotherapy improves strength that also helps after surgery.

blocks.text: Your surgeon will confirm the timing that suits you.

sections.heading: What happens to the C-section scar?

blocks.text: In most cases the Tummy Tuck incision is placed low on the abdomen, close to where a caesarean scar sits. The skin removed during surgery often includes the old C-section scar, so it is taken away and replaced by a new one.
How the Tummy Tuck scar compares

items: **Position:** low, usually hidden by underwear or a swimsuit. Your surgeon will mark it with you before surgery.
**Length:** usually longer than a C-section scar, as it often runs towards the hip bones on each side. The length depends on how much loose skin needs removing.
**Belly button:** a full Tummy Tuck also leaves a small scar around the repositioned belly button.
**Healing:** the NHS notes that scars are raised and red at first and usually fade over 12 to 18 months.

blocks.text: If your C-section scar sits unusually high, or you have more than one scar, discuss how they will be handled. Not every scar can be removed completely.

sections.heading: Full vs Mini Tummy Tuck: which suits you?

head: Feature
Full Tummy Tuck
Mini Tummy Tuck
rows: Loose skin above and below the belly button, muscle separation, a pronounced overhang
Small amount of loose skin below the belly button only
Low hip-to-hip incision plus a scar around the belly button
Shorter low incision; belly button usually untouched
Full length, above and below the belly button
Usually only below the belly button

blocks.text: Many women after pregnancy need a full Tummy Tuck because the muscle separation runs above the belly button too. A Mini Tummy Tuck suits a smaller group with a limited lower overhang and good muscle tone.

sections.heading: Muscle repair and Diastasis Recti

blocks.text: During pregnancy, the two vertical "six-pack" muscles can separate. This is called Diastasis Recti (separation of the abdominal muscles). During a full Tummy Tuck, the surgeon stitches the stretched midline together, which narrows the waist and flattens the lower belly. If an umbilical hernia is present, it can usually be repaired at the same time. To learn more, read our guide to [Diastasis Recti: exercises vs surgical repair](/blog/diastasis-recti-exercises-vs-surgery).

sections.heading: Who is a good candidate (and who is not)?

blocks.text: You may be a good candidate if you:

items: Have loose lower abdominal skin, an overhang or muscle separation after pregnancy
Have completed your family and finished breastfeeding
Are at or near a stable, healthy weight
Are a non-smoker, or are willing to stop well before and after surgery
Have realistic expectations about scars and results

blocks.text: A Tummy Tuck after C-section may not be right for you now if you:

items: Plan to become pregnant again
Are still within the first months after delivery
Have significant weight still to lose
Have uncontrolled diabetes or high blood pressure, or a history of blood clots that has not been assessed
Feel pressured by others to "get your body back"

sections.heading: The procedure: what to expect

items: **Consultation:** examination of skin, fat, muscles and your existing scar, plus a review of your pregnancies, deliveries and health.
**Planning:** deciding between full and Mini Tummy Tuck, muscle repair, and whether Liposuction is added.
**Preparation:** blood tests, anaesthesia check, stopping smoking, and planning childcare and help at home.
**Anaesthesia:** a Tummy Tuck is performed under general anaesthesia.

**Surgery:** the surgeon removes excess skin and fat, repairs the muscles, repositions the belly button (in a full Tummy Tuck) and closes in layers. Drains may be placed. It usually takes around two to four hours.
**Hospital stay:** often one or two nights, with early walking to reduce clot risk.

blocks.text: Can it be combined with other procedures?

A Tummy Tuck can be combined with procedures such as [Liposuction](/liposuction-surgery-bangalore) or breast surgery, sometimes called a "mommy makeover". This means one anaesthetic and one recovery period. However, research reported by the American Society of Plastic Surgeons found that complication risk is higher when Abdominoplasty is combined with other procedures. Your surgeon should weigh this carefully.
Can I have a Tummy Tuck during my C-section?

Combining the two is generally not recommended. After pregnancy, the tissues are swollen and stretched, which makes the result unpredictable and may increase healing problems. Most surgeons prefer to wait until you have fully recovered.

sections.heading: Tummy Tuck recovery time: a phase-by-phase guide

blocks.text: Everyone heals differently, and your surgeon's instructions come first. As a general guide:

head: Phase
What is normal
Typical restrictions and milestones
rows: Tightness, pain controlled with medicines, swelling, walking slightly bent
Short walks several times a day, compression garment, drain care if used, no lifting
Pain eases; you begin standing straighter
Desk work often from 2 to 3 weeks; no lifting your child or heavy objects until cleared
Driving when you can brake and twist comfortably; gradual return to exercise around 6 weeks if advised
Final shape emerges; scar flattens and fades
Scar care and sun protection; core strengthening as guided

blocks.text: The NHS advises around 4 to 6 weeks off work and exercise, and wearing a support garment for about six weeks. The ASPS notes that most patients begin to feel more normal at about eight weeks.

sections.heading: Risks and complications

blocks.text: A Tummy Tuck after C-section is major surgery. Possible risks include:

items: Bleeding or haematoma
Infection
Seroma (fluid collection under the skin)
Delayed wound healing or wound breakdown, especially in smokers
Thick, raised or widened scars, and small "dog ears" at the scar ends
Numbness of the lower abdomen, which can last months or longer
Blood clots in the legs (DVT) or lungs
Asymmetry or a result that differs from expectations, sometimes needing revision surgery

blocks.text: Your surgeon will discuss how to reduce these risks before you consent.

sections.heading: Tummy Tuck cost in India

blocks.text: The cost of a Tummy Tuck in India depends on:

items: **Full or Mini Tummy Tuck,** and whether muscle repair, hernia repair or Liposuction are added
**Surgeon's experience** with post-pregnancy body contouring
**Hospital category and stay,** usually one or two nights
**Anaesthesia** fees
**City:** Bangalore and other metros are generally higher
**Extras:** compression garments, tests and medicines

blocks.text: As an approximate guide, this practice lists a typical uncomplicated Tummy Tuck at INR 3,50,000 to 4,50,000 plus GST. Pre-operative tests, medicines after discharge and compression garments are usually billed separately. See our [treatment costs page](/treatment-costs) for current details.

sections.heading: When to call your surgeon

blocks.text: Contact your surgeon promptly if you have:

items: Fever above 38 degrees C, or chills
Spreading redness, warmth, pus or a bad smell from the wound
The wound opening or skin turning dark
Sudden, severe swelling or pain on one side
Calf pain or swelling, chest pain or breathlessness. Seek emergency care

sections.heading: Questions to ask at your consultation

items: Do I need a full or Mini Tummy Tuck, and why?
Will my C-section scar be removed, and how long will the new scar be?
Do I have muscle separation or a hernia that needs repair?
How long should I wait after delivery and breastfeeding?
Is it safe to combine this with other procedures in my case?
Which hospital and how many nights? What does the cost include?
What help will I need at home with my child?

sections.heading: Is a Tummy Tuck after C section right for you?

blocks.text: A Tummy Tuck after C section can address the overhang, loose skin and muscle separation that exercise cannot change, and it usually replaces the old scar with a carefully placed new one. Timing it well, after your family is complete and your body has recovered, gives the most lasting result. Read more about [Tummy Tuck surgery in Bangalore](/tummy-tuck-abdominoplasty-bangalore), explore other [body contouring options](/body-plastic-surgeon-bangalore), learn about [Dr Vybhav Deraje](/aboutus), and [book a consultation](/contact-us) when you are ready.

faqs.q: How long after a C-section can I get a Tummy Tuck?
faqs.a: Most surgeons advise waiting at least 6 to 12 months after a C-section. You should also have finished breastfeeding, reached a stable weight and completed your family. This gives the scar and abdominal wall time to heal fully and lets your surgeon judge what surgery will truly add.

faqs.q: Does a Tummy Tuck remove the C-section scar?
faqs.a: Often, yes. The Tummy Tuck incision is usually placed near the C-section scar, and the old scar is commonly removed with the excess skin. The new scar is usually longer, running towards the hips, but sits low and is designed to be hidden by underwear. Results depend on where your scar sits.

faqs.q: Can a Tummy Tuck fix the C-section overhang?
faqs.a: Yes. A Tummy Tuck removes the excess skin and fat that form the overhang and releases the scar that tethers the skin. With muscle repair, it also flattens the lower belly. Liposuction may be added for shape. Exercise alone cannot remove this fold because it involves stretched skin.

faqs.q: Can I get pregnant after a Tummy Tuck?
faqs.a: Yes, a Tummy Tuck does not affect fertility, and pregnancy after Abdominoplasty is possible. However, pregnancy will stretch the skin and muscle repair again and may undo much of the result. That is why surgeons recommend waiting until your family is complete. A future C-section can still be performed after a Tummy Tuck.

faqs.q: How long is Tummy Tuck recovery time?
faqs.a: Most people need 2 to 3 weeks before desk work and about 6 weeks before strenuous exercise or heavy lifting. Many feel close to normal by around eight weeks. Swelling continues to settle for several months, and the scar matures over 12 to 18 months. Your surgeon will give a personal plan.

faqs.q: Is a Tummy Tuck after C-section safe?
faqs.a: For healthy, well-selected patients, a Tummy Tuck after C-section is generally safe when performed by a qualified plastic surgeon in an accredited hospital. It is still major surgery, with risks such as seroma, infection, wound healing problems and blood clots. Not smoking, a stable weight and following aftercare instructions help reduce risk.

faqs.q: Can I combine a Tummy Tuck with breast surgery?
faqs.a: Yes, a Tummy Tuck is sometimes combined with breast surgery or Liposuction in one operation, often called a mommy makeover. This means a single recovery, but complication risk is higher with combined procedures. Your surgeon will consider your health, the length of surgery and your support at home before advising.

disclaimer: This article is for general education only. It is not medical advice or a diagnosis, and it does not replace a consultation with a qualified plastic surgeon. Individual plans vary, and results differ from person to person.
